title: Recharge your survival systems
what: Watch the two bars (Life Support and Hazard Protection). Refill Life Support with Oxygen (red plants) and recharge Hazard Protection with Sodium (yellow plants).
why: Both drain whenever you are outside your ship, and hitting zero starts draining your health. Survival comes before everything else.
tip: Ducking into a cave pauses environmental hazards completely — a free way to wait out storms.

title: Mine the three starter resources
what: Use the mining beam on rocks for Ferrite Dust, on plants for Carbon, and on blue crystals for Di-hydrogen.
why: These three cover almost every early repair, craft and fuel need.
tip: Carbon refuels the mining beam itself — never let it run dry far from plants.

title: Repair the Analysis Visor and scan
what: Repair the Analysis Visor with the materials prompted, then scan plants and animals around you.
why: Scanning pays out units instantly and is your very first source of income.
tip: Scan everything new — full fauna scans on a planet pay a bonus.

title: Repair and fuel your starship
what: Follow the markers to repair the Pulse Engine and Launch Thrusters (Metal Plating needs ~50 Ferrite Dust; thrusters need Pure Ferrite + Di-hydrogen Jelly). Refuel the launch thrusters.
why: You cannot leave the starting planet without a working, fuelled ship.
tip: Refine Ferrite Dust 1:1 into Pure Ferrite, and 40 Di-hydrogen into Di-hydrogen Jelly, in a portable refiner.

title: Learn how to save
what: Hop out of your ship to create a restore point, or interact with any beacon at a structure.
why: There is no "save and quit" — unsaved progress is lost when you close the game.
tip: Make exiting the ship a habit before you ever quit.

title: Fly to a space station
what: Take off and fly to the space station icon in the system.
why: Stations are your hub for trading, upgrades, missions, fuel and saving.
tip: The Pulse Engine (fuelled by Tritium from asteroids) makes in-system travel fast.

title: Earn your first units
what: Sell surplus resources at the Galactic Trade Terminal, and dig up Buried Technology (a Wi-Fi-like scan icon) for Salvaged Data.
why: Units fund inventory slots, technology and fuel — your main early bottleneck.
tip: Salvaged Data sells well, unlocks blueprints, and refines into nanites — collect plenty.

title: Visit the Space Anomaly
what: Once unlocked, summon the Anomaly from the quick menu while in space and go aboard.
why: Nada and Polo sell key blueprints and upgrades for nanites, and the Nexus offers missions.
tip: Pick up early exosuit and tech blueprints here — they pay for themselves quickly.

title: Expand your Exosuit inventory
what: Buy a slot at the suit terminal on the station, and claim free slots from Drop Pods on planets (scan for them).
why: A cramped early inventory is the single biggest beginner frustration.
tip: The first suit slot is cheap (~5,000 units); buy at least one every station visit.

title: Start earning Nanites
what: Refine Salvaged Data (~15 each) or Runaway Mould (5:1) into Nanite Clusters; later, buy and scrap cheap ships.
why: Nanites are the second currency, used for upgrade modules and blueprints.
tip: Units and nanites are spent in different shops — don't mix them up.

title: Upgrade or swap your Multi-Tool
what: Check Multi-Tool cabinets at trading posts and stations; buy or claim one with more slots and a stronger beam.
why: A better tool mines, scans and fights faster, speeding up everything else.
tip: Reloading a save reshuffles which tool a cabinet offers.

title: Build a Hyperdrive and craft Warp Cells
what: Get and install the Hyperdrive blueprint, then craft a Warp Cell from Antimatter + Antimatter Housing.
why: Warp Cells let you leave your starting system and continue the story.
tip: Antimatter = Chromatic Metal + Condensed Carbon; the story hands you the recipe.

title: Start your first base
what: Craft and place a Base Computer (needs Chromatic Metal) and activate it to claim the area.
why: A base gives storage, refiners, a teleporter and a steady drip of free blueprints.
tip: Choose a calm planet — no extreme weather or aggressive Sentinels — with resources nearby.

title: Unlock building blueprints
what: Build a Construction Research Station and trade Salvaged Data for building plans.
why: This unlocks storage, doors, refiners and decoration you will reuse everywhere.
tip: Over-collected Salvaged Data refines into nanites, so it is never wasted.

title: Set up storage and a refiner
what: Build Storage Containers and a Refiner at your base.
why: Stored items are never lost on death, and refining turns raw resources into profit and craft materials.
tip: Deposit valuables before risky trips — your grave only holds what you were carrying.

title: Install upgrades with adjacency in mind
what: Put upgrade modules in the Technology section and cluster matching ones together, next to the core tech.
why: Adjacent related upgrades grant a bonus, so placement noticeably boosts performance.
tip: Watch for the highlighted links shown while installing to confirm the bonus.

title: Claim a free Freighter
what: Keep warping; answer a freighter distress call and defeat the attacking pirate waves.
why: A freighter is a mobile base with big storage and frigate fleet missions.
tip: Decline payment on the first offer and the next free freighter is often larger. (unsicher: über Updates angepasst)

title: Build a basic income loop
what: Pick one: Chlorine + Oxygen refining, Activated Indium mining, or buy-low/sell-high trade runs.
why: A steady income lets you buy slots, ships and tech without grinding.
tip: A few automated extractors or refiners earn while you are off exploring.

title: Keep following the main missions
what: Continue the Artemis Path (and dip into the Atlas Path) from your mission log.
why: Story missions hand out free blueprints and unlock systems and features you cannot reach otherwise.
tip: Do most main missions before wandering off — some unlocks are story-gated.
